u0: Ordinary progress: the exit has not yet been reached and no box fall is awaiting an immediate recovery. The box may be in your hands or, after an earlier fall, put down somewhere; either way, success still requires reaching the exit with the box in hand. If the box slips from your grasp, you must be holding it again on the very next step.
u1: A fall has just occurred while the exit has not been reached, so the immediate-recovery requirement is pending. On the very next step you must be holding the box again; doing so returns you to ordinary progress, while doing so on the exit step completes the task. If you are not holding it on that next step, the mandatory rule is broken and the task fails.
u2: The exit has been reached while the box was not in your hands, so the requirement to have the box at the exit is not yet satisfied. This is not an immediate failure: the task can still complete if you come to hold the box on a later step without a new fall. Remaining empty-handed leaves the objective unresolved.
u3: The task is complete: the exit has been reached and the box is held as required, with no immediate fall-recovery obligation outstanding. No further action is needed.
u4: The exit has been reached without the box in hand, and a fall has just been recorded while the box was out of hand, so both the box-at-exit condition and the immediate pickup are outstanding. The next step must leave you holding the box without another fall, which completes the task. If you remain empty-handed on that next step, or another fall is recorded without the box in hand, the task fails.
u5: A fall has been recorded together with the box being held, so an immediate recovery check is still pending even though the box is shown in hand; the exit has also already been reached. One more step holding the box without a new fall completes the task. If the box is not in hand on that step, or another fall is recorded without the box in hand, the task fails.
u6: A mandatory requirement has been violated: the box was not in hand on the required next step after a fall, leaving the immediate-recovery obligation unmet. Successful completion is no longer possible; the task is failed.
